questions.question: According to the law of demand, other things being equal:
options: A rise in price reduces the quantity demanded
A rise in price increases the quantity demanded
Quantity demanded is fixed regardless of price
Demand depends only on advertising

questions.question: A learner who dreams of the newest phone but has no savings:
options: Adds nothing to demand — demand requires being willing AND able to pay
Counts as demand because wanting is enough
Shifts the demand curve rightward
Raises the equilibrium price

questions.question: The price of eggs itself rises and shoppers buy fewer. On the diagram this is:
options: A leftward shift of the entire demand curve
A movement along the same demand curve — a change in quantity demanded
A rightward shift of the demand curve
A movement along the supply curve

questions.question: Which change would shift the whole demand curve for eggs to the RIGHT?
options: A fall in the price of eggs
A rise in the price of eggs
A rise in household incomes
Bird flu striking the laying farms

questions.question: The supply curve slopes upward because:
options: Producers enjoy drawing rising lines
A higher price is a stronger incentive, so producers offer more
Buyers demand more at higher prices
Costs disappear at high prices

questions.question: Bird flu culls millions of laying hens. Why does this SHIFT the supply curve rather than move along it?
options: Because the change was caused by disease, not by the egg price
Because every change in a market shifts a curve
Because buyers changed their tastes at the same time
Because eggs are sold in trays

questions.question: After the outbreak, the egg supply curve moves:
options: Rightward — more offered at every price
Leftward — fewer eggs offered at every price
Nowhere; only demand moves
It becomes vertical at zero

questions.question: Which of the following would shift the supply curve of eggs RIGHTWARD?
options: A jump in the price of chicken feed
A new levy on egg producers
New hen housing that raises laying rates at the same cost
Another disease outbreak

questions.question: At the equilibrium price:
options: Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied and the market clears
Sellers always hold some unsold stock
The state fixes the price by law
Buyers outnumber sellers

questions.question: If the market price sits ABOVE equilibrium:
options: A shortage appears and the price rises further
A surplus appears — unsold stock pushes sellers to cut the price toward equilibrium
Both curves shift leftward
The price stays there permanently

questions.question: A price BELOW equilibrium creates:
options: A surplus, so the price falls
Instant market clearing
A shortage — competing buyers bid the price up toward equilibrium
A shift of the demand curve

subtopics.title: The Bird Flu Diagram — Working the Full Example

questions.question: In the bird flu example, the demand curve stays put because:
options: Demand curves can never move
Household incomes and tastes are unchanged
The outbreak reduced demand as well
The egg price shifted demand instead

questions.question: Comparing the new equilibrium with the old one after supply shifts left:
options: Price is higher and the quantity traded is smaller
Price is lower and the quantity traded is larger
Both price and quantity are higher
Both price and quantity are unchanged

questions.question: At the OLD price, immediately after supply shifts left, the egg market shows:
options: A surplus of eggs
A shortage — quantity demanded exceeds the reduced quantity supplied
Perfect balance
Falling prices

questions.question: As the egg price climbs toward the new equilibrium, households cutting back on eggs appears on the diagram as:
options: A leftward shift of the demand curve
A movement along the unchanged demand curve
A rightward shift of supply
A brand-new demand curve

subtopics.title: The Vetkoek Table at the School Gate

questions.question: The boy staring at the vetkoek table with empty pockets:
options: Is not part of demand — demand is hunger PLUS money ready: willing AND able
Counts as demand because he is hungry
Shifts the supply curve leftward
Determines the equilibrium price

questions.question: At twelve rand, gogo calls her daughter to help fry more vetkoek because:
options: Frying is easier with company
Price is the seller's payslip — a better price pulls more supply to the gate
Demand always rises when price rises
The dough was about to expire

questions.question: The two laws "pull against each other" because:
options: Buyers and sellers refuse to meet
Both curves slope downward
Cheaper draws MORE buyers while dearer draws MORE sellers — opposite pulls that must settle somewhere
The school sets the price

questions.question: At twelve rand, the stack of cold vetkoek going stiff under the cloth is the street version of:
options: A SURPLUS — quantity supplied exceeding quantity demanded, pushing the price down
A shortage
Market equilibrium
A demand shift

questions.question: At four rand, the bare table and the queue still stretching mean:
options: The price will drop again tomorrow
A SHORTAGE — quantity demanded exceeding quantity supplied, pulling tomorrow's price up
The market has cleared perfectly
Supply has shifted rightward

questions.question: Equilibrium is the morning that "works perfectly" because:
options: Gogo earns her highest possible profit
The price is at its highest
The last vetkoek sells to the last willing buyer — nothing left over, nobody sent away
The queue never ends

questions.question: "Nobody chose that price" refers to:
options: Prices being set at random
Gogo forgetting her price list
The school governing body's decision
Price formation through market forces — thousands of small choices settling it between them

subtopics.title: The Egg Shelf at the Spaza

questions.question: The two diagnostic questions to ask about any market shock are:
options: WHOSE side of the market got hit, and did the good's OWN price cause it?
How long will it last, and who is to blame?
Is it imported, and is it taxed?
What did the newspapers say, and when?

questions.question: The outbreak shifts the whole egg supply curve left because:
options: The egg price caused the culling
At EVERY price there are fewer eggs to offer — a virus changed the sellers' world, not the price
Shoppers suddenly disliked eggs
Farmers slid along their old curve

questions.question: As the egg price climbs after the outbreak, the two simultaneous movements are:
options: Both curves shifting a second time
Demand shifting left while supply shifts right
Buyers sliding along their unchanged demand curve (beans, smaller cartons) and sellers stretching along the NEW supply curve
No movements — the market freezes

questions.question: The new resting place after the outbreak shows:
options: A lower price and more eggs traded
The same price and fewer eggs
A lower price and fewer eggs
A HIGHER price and FEWER eggs traded — exactly what the country saw at the shops
